Cargo

Contrôle de la viscosité

The process of monitoring and adjusting the viscosity of liquid cargo, often by heating or blending, to ensure efficient transfer and compliance with charter requirements.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Contrôle de la viscosité?

In this glossary, Contrôle de la viscosité refers to: The process of monitoring and adjusting the viscosity of liquid cargo, often by heating or blending, to ensure efficient transfer and compliance with charter requirements.

How is Contrôle de la viscosité used in maritime?

In maritime communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Ingénieur de cargaison à la veille du pont : Maintenez la température de la cargaison selon le plan de contrôle de la viscosité."

Why does Contrôle de la viscosité matter in maritime?

Contrôle de la viscosité matters because it supports clear communication in Cargo contexts for Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as STCW, Marlins Test, ISF Watchkeeper, and GMDSS.

Who uses Contrôle de la viscosité?

Contrôle de la viscosité is mainly used by Deck Officers, Engine Officers, and Masters.

What category does Contrôle de la viscosité belong to?

In this glossary, Contrôle de la viscosité is grouped under Cargo. Related pages in this category explain adjacent procedures, commands and operational concepts.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from IMO SMCP, STCW Convention, SOLAS, COLREG and published by Protermify Maritime as a static maritime reference page.

Definition

The process of monitoring and adjusting the viscosity of liquid cargo, often by heating or blending, to ensure efficient transfer and compliance with charter requirements.

Operational example

Cargo engineer to deck watch: Maintain cargo temperature as per viscosity control plan for optimal discharge.

Localized term

Contrôle de la viscosité

Localized example
